items.title: remove_stored/rename_stored throw after the change is done when the parent-directory fsync fails, and a retried remove_stored fails with ENOENT
items.role: Honest operator (storing machines) per AUDIT.md row 1; callers in this repo (PRT player, CLI stored revert) are Support
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: the only trigger is a failing fsync(2) (EIO), a host fault. Section 8: 'Host faults, such as a full disk, as long as the emulator does not turn them into a wrong hash, a wrong proof, or a directory that O2 guarantees but that later loads as a different state'. No hash, proof or guaranteed directory is affected; the removed directory is no longer a snapshot. Stop. If read as in scope: 3 the Medium persistence case needs 'an uncommon host setup that the manual documents, or while cleaning up after a stop', neither of which is a transient in-process fault; 4 no rule (R9, O2) violated; the player recovers via its fs.exists guard; 5 Low.
items.reason: Trigger is a host fault (fsync EIO) with no wrong hash, proof or damaged O2-guaranteed directory: section 8 host-fault exclusion. Otherwise Low: violates no rule; the Medium persistence case needs a documented uncommon host setup or post-stop cleanup.

items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: not excluded as such; the caller is trusted. 2 Role: Support library; section 3 'A library stands in for the most critical role among the components that reach the defect through it'. Checked every in-tree caller (src/cartesi-machine.lua, src/cartesi/hash-tree.lua, doc/recipes/prt.lua, game-transport.lua, cartesi-rollup-data.lua): all pass constant indents -1 or 2, so no component reaches the defect. The C API and JSON-RPC always dump with -1. 3 The High/Critical memory-safety cases need 'data from other parties'; the indent is never such data. 4 No rule violated at a reachable state or on the honest path. 5 Low: 'a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller' / a real defect that violates no rule.
items.reason: Indent comes only from trusted callers' constants (-1 or 2 at every in-tree call site, checked); never data from other parties, so section 4/8 memory-safety cases do not apply; no component reaches it; section 8 Low.

items.title: yield utility resolves reasons independently of mode: 'manual tx-output' gives rx-rejected, 'manual progress' rx-accepted, 'automatic rx-accepted' progress
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: application-design exclusion does not apply to a guest-software defect, continue. 2 Role: Guest software; section 3 'in scope only where an application depends on them as documented, and would be correctly designed if they worked as documented ... Any other defect in them is Low'. The manual documents /usr/bin/yield only for 'automatic progress <permil>' (doc/README.md ~2726); cross-mode pairs have no documented meaning, and at the HTIF level manual reason 1/2/4 are rx-accepted/rx-rejected/tx-exception, so an application issuing 'manual progress' would not be correctly designed even if the tool did exactly what it asked. 3 none. 4 The Critical clause needs an input to make a documented-use application deviate (readings: decide on documented/intended use); no documented-use application reaches it. 5 Low.
items.reason: Only an application invoking undocumented cross-mode pairs reaches it; section 3 guest software in scope only for documented use, 'Any other defect in them is Low'; section 8 Low 'defect in guest software that only an application outside its intended use can reach'.

items.title: PRT bridge retires an epoch on the 'latest' nonce; a within-policy reorg resurrects its transaction as an orphaned pending candidate that blocks every live epoch's moves
items.component: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:tick (retirement 702-710, other-epoch early return 720-727), prt-transactions.lua methods:pending/nonce ('latest'), crisium.lua pass()
items.role: Support (PRT bridge), standing in for the honest operator's transaction submission
items.severity: Medium (preferred: support stand-in for a Critical R4/A7 violation) / Out of scope (if section 4's 'Acting on history before it is final, and recovering when that history is replaced, is outside this model' covers a shallow reorg of the operator's own transaction) / Low (if condition 3 is read as a trusted-node fault)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: section 8 excludes only reorgs 'deeper than the operator's input policy'; this one is shallower than both policies. Reading A (in scope): section 4 'The honest operator acts only on history that its policy treats as final'; the bridge breaks it by retiring on the 'latest' nonce, while the journal itself says 'A reorg can resurrect every nonce up to high_water'. Reading B: the pre-finality sentence of section 4 excludes recovery. The node dropping the reorged tx could be a trusted-node behaviour, but the fee-spike variant uses chain activity the adversary may raise (section 7) and races are an adversary capability. 2 Role: Support bridge (AUDIT.md), stand-in honest operator ('Submitting transactions'). 3 Section 3 'Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. In the stood-in role the live epoch's moves are never sent: R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks' and 'defends every epoch whose dispute is open'; the honest claim loses by timeout (completeness failure). Step 4 there is Critical, so Medium. Code checked: tick retires when pending() (nonce at 'latest', prt-transactions.lua:35) returns no candidate of this epoch; other bridges return early on any other-epoch candidate (720-727); crisium drops finished bridges. Distinct from R1-A8-4 (same-epoch pending preference, different trigger and fix) and R5-INVBRIDGE-2 (crash on pinned-block reorg).
items.reason: Kept: in scope under the reading that the bridge itself acts on non-final history (section 4); support stand-in for a Critical R4 completeness failure gives Medium (section 3). Out of scope only under the pre-finality reading. Code facts verified.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: the PRT bridge (doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua methods:tick, lines ~702-710) marks a settled epoch finished when it has no jobs and transactions:pending(signer) (doc/recipes/prt-transactions.lua methods:pending, which reads eth_getTransactionCount at 'latest', line 35) returns no candidate of this epoch, and the settlement block is <= head(retirement_policy). crisium.lua pass() (~318-331) then drops that bridge. The journal keeps every nonce up to high_water until forget_settled sees a receipt at or below finality ('A reorg can resurrect every nonce up to high_water'). If the retired epoch's last own transaction C (e.g. tryRecoveringBond, after another party's identical call already removed the job at the 4-deep observation head) sits above the observation head and a shallow reorg (within dispute depth 4 and input policy) removes C's block and C is not re-mined (dropped, or base fee above its max fee), pending() again returns C with context.epoch = X. Every live epoch's bridge hits 'if candidate.context and candidate.context.epoch ~= tostring(self.epoch) then return snapshot, false, next_block end' (lines ~720-727) forever: no join, bisection or proof of the live dispute is sent; no error, so prt-supervise.sh does not relaunch. With --keep-epochs=0 a relaunch does not reopen X either. Required behavior: R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks' and 'defends every epoch whose dispute is open'; section 4 'The honest operator acts only on history that its policy treats as final'; section 3 support stand-in rule ('Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'). Test idea (hunter): deterministic Lua test with the real prt-transactions journal and two real prt-bridge instances (observe/refresh/jobs/prepare stubbed) against an in-process fake node: retire epoch 1 while its mined copy is above the observation head, reorg 4 blocks dropping that tx, give epoch 2 a due move, assert epoch 2's move is published and mined within its window (exit 1 today; 0 once retirement waits for the epoch's candidates to settle, or live bridges adopt/cancel orphaned candidates). Also cover the fee-spike variant (re-injected but underpriced), which avoids relying on a node that drops reorged txs. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/DYNBRIDGE/scenario-wedge.lua and fakechain.lua (outputs 'after reorg tip 18 pending e1-recover@0', 'tip 70: epoch-2 move [40,60) done=nil', variants 'keep spike' and RESTART=keep0 exit 1; 'keep' and RESTART=keep1 recover); hunter file /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/hunt-DYNBRIDGE.json #1.

items.title: PRT epoch listener aborts crisium ('epoch log history was truncated') when a within-policy reorg to a shorter branch lowers the numeric observation head over still-canonical applied inputs
items.component: doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua methods:poll (line ~52 assert) with prt-log-history.lua observe() rewind to min(common_ancestor, head)
items.role: Support (PRT player listener), standing in for the honest operator's chain observation and input delivery
items.severity: Medium (if a crash on a within-policy chain event that replaces no history the operator acted on is a stood-in R4 Critical) / Low (preferred by hunter: relaunch recovers, as in R3-VARO2PLAYER-1 and R5-INVBRIDGE-2)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: the reorg is shallower than the input policy and leaves every block at or below the old observation head canonical, so neither 'Reorganizations ... deeper than the operator's input policy' nor section 4's 'recovering when that history is replaced' applies: the history the listener applied was not replaced. A node whose 'latest' goes backward without a reorg would be a trusted-node quirk. 2 Role: Support listener, stand-in honest operator ('Observing the chain', 'Delivering inputs'). 3 Section 3 stand-in rule. Reading A: a crash of the honest operator on a normal in-policy chain event (chain data relayed by the node) violates R4 'observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks' on the honest path, Critical in that role, so Medium. Reading B: R4's restart clause is met (a fresh listener polls fine) and A7 budgets no restart time, so Low, as the readings of R3-VARO2PLAYER-1 and R5-INVBRIDGE-2. Deciding facts: relaunch cost (reopen every epoch, refetch logs, reload stored players) versus clocks, and repetition frequency. Code checked: poll asserts #logs >= #self.applied after observe() rewinds to min(common_ancestor, head). Distinct site and fix from R5-INVBRIDGE-2 (journal nonce/preflight pin).
items.reason: Kept as unsure: unlike R5-INVBRIDGE-2, the applied history stays canonical and final under the operator's own policy, so the pre-finality exclusion does not obviously apply; Medium under the stood-in R4 crash reading, Low under the restart-recovers reading.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: with a numeric --input-policy d (the recipe demo uses PRT_INPUT_CONFIRMATIONS default 8; crisium documents --input-policy=POLICY), prt-epoch.lua methods:poll takes head = chain:head(input_policy) = tip - d, calls history:observe(head), and prt-log-history.lua observe() rewinds to math.min(common_ancestor(self), head), dropping logs of blocks above a lower new head even when they are still canonical. poll then asserts '#logs >= #self.applied' ('epoch log history was truncated', line ~52) and the error propagates out of crisium's pass, killing the player. Trigger: a reorg whose fork point is above the old observation head and whose new branch is shorter (tip number decreases), with at least one applied InputAdded in a block between new and old head. Required behavior: R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks'; section 4 'The honest operator acts only on history that its policy treats as final' (the applied block remains canonical); section 3 support stand-in rule. A lower observation head over unchanged history must not be treated as truncation: poll should return without delivering, and once the head returns, deliver no input twice and lose none. Test idea (hunter): drive the real prt-epoch.lua, prt-log-history.lua and prt-rpc.lua head/is_canonical/logs against a scripted chain (or anvil with a reorg to a shorter branch above the observation head), input_policy = 8; inputs in blocks 10, 11, 12; poll at tip 20 (head 12) applies 3; reorg depth 2 replaced by 1 block (tip 19, head 11, block 12 still canonical); assert poll() does not raise, then advance the tip and assert all 3 inputs are applied exactly once. Control: equal-length branch polls ok. Exit 1 today at prt-epoch.lua:52. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/DYNBRIDGE/scenario-listener.lua and fakechain.lua; hunter file /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/hunt-DYNBRIDGE.json #2.

items.title: crisium's WebSocket head subscription reads the rest of a started frame with no timeout, so a mid-frame network stall hangs the player forever with no crash to relaunch
items.component: doc/recipes/prt-websocket.lua methods:receive (settimeout(nil) after the first byte, lines ~78-109) / subscription wait, called from crisium.lua main loop with --ws
items.role: Support (PRT player), standing in for the honest operator's chain observation
items.severity: Out of scope (preferred: network/host fault between the operator and its trusted node) / Medium (if a transient fault turned into a permanent, supervisor-invisible hang of the stood-in honest operator violates R4's restart clause; same open reading as R5-INVPLAYER-1)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: the trigger is a network fault or stalled proxy between the player and its own node; section 4 trusts 'the operator's host, keys, and node' and says 'A host fault ... may stop the honest operator', and section 8 excludes host faults that do not become a wrong hash, proof or guaranteed directory. Preferred: Out of scope. Counter-reading: the fault is transient but the hang is permanent and silent, so the operator never 'restarts ... and keeps defending its claim' (R4); this is the gap recorded for R5-INVPLAYER-1, whose reviewer gave Medium as the alternative, pending the second opinion. 2 Role: Support, stand-in honest operator. 3 Stand-in R4 violation would be Critical, giving Medium. Code checked: prt-websocket.lua line 87 sets settimeout(nil) once a frame starts; no keepalive.
items.reason: Kept as unsure: the host/network-fault exclusion likely applies, but a transient fault becoming a permanent silent hang is the open reading of R5-INVPLAYER-1 (Medium alternative). Code fact verified (settimeout(nil) mid-frame).
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: doc/recipes/prt-websocket.lua methods:receive sets self.tcp:settimeout(timeout) only for the first byte of a frame (line ~81) and then settimeout(nil) (line ~87) for the rest ('Once a message starts, the rest is read without a timeout'); no TCP keepalive is set. crisium.lua's idle branch calls heads:wait(poll_interval) (lines ~359, 375-380) expecting it to return within the poll interval. If the connection stalls mid-frame without FIN/RST (half-open TCP, NAT drop, stalled proxy), wait never returns and crisium's single thread stops observing, ticking and submitting; no error is raised, so prt-supervise.sh never relaunches. Required behavior (contested): R4 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks' and 'After a stop, it restarts ... and keeps defending its claim'; section 4 'A host fault ... may stop the honest operator'. The test should assert that subscription:wait(1) returns (nil or an error) within a bound such as 2x the timeout, or that crisium reads the tip within its poll interval. Note for the reviewer: the preferred rating is Out of scope under the host-fault exclusion; Medium only under the R5-INVPLAYER-1 alternative reading. Test idea (hunter): two processes on 127.0.0.1: a fake node completes the RFC 6455 handshake and the eth_subscribe reply, sends one byte (0x81) of the next text frame, then stays silent with the socket open; the client is the real prt-websocket new_head_subscription followed by heads:wait(1); assert return within ~2 s (exit 1 today: still blocked after 5.5 s). Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/DYNBRIDGE/ws-stall.lua; hunter file /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/hunt-DYNBRIDGE.json #3.

threat_model_gaps: Within-policy reorgs of the operator's own transactions: section 4 says the honest operator acts only on final history and excludes 'Acting on history before it is final, and recovering when that history is replaced', but transaction submission necessarily acts at the tip; unclear whether a shallow reorg that drops the operator's own mined transaction (and a retirement decision taken on the 'latest' nonce) is covered (R6-DYNBRIDGE-1; related to R5-INVBRIDGE-2).

Lowered observation head over unchanged history: a reorg to a shorter branch that replaces no block the operator acted on, but crashes it, is neither a reorg deeper than the policy nor a replacement of acted-on history; with A7 silent on restart time, a crash followed by a successful restart has no clear class (R6-DYNBRIDGE-2; extends the R5-INVBRIDGE-2 and R3-VARO2PLAYER-1 gaps).

Transient host/network faults that become a permanent, silent hang: section 4 lets a host fault 'stop the honest operator' and R4 requires a restart after a stop, but the model does not say whether operator software that hangs undetectably (defeating the restart) is covered by the host-fault exclusion (R6-DYNBRIDGE-3; same gap as R5-INVPLAYER-1).

Persistence calls that cannot be completed after an in-process host fault: the Medium persistence case covers only 'an uncommon host setup that the manual documents, or while cleaning up after a stop'; a call whose documented retry cannot succeed after a transient fault (no wrong hash, no damaged guaranteed directory) falls to the host-fault exclusion or Low without a stated reading (R6-DYNPERSIST-1).

R3 'trailing data' versus ignored or contradictory header fields and non-canonical encodings: the Medium/Low trailing-data case names only trailing data; whether ignored brackets/notes, log_type flags contradicting the log, or whitespace-tolerant base64 (log malleability: two byte-different logs verify) count as 'trailing data that does not affect its result' or as other log-validity conditions that R3 says 'must be rejected' is not stated (R6-DYNLOGFUZZ-1).

Guest-tool documented use when the help text admits combinations the protocol encodes identically: yield.c's help lists modes and reasons independently; section 3's 'depends on them as documented' does not say whether every combination a tool's own help accepts is documented use (R6-DYNGUEST-1).

Latent memory-safety defects in support libraries reachable only through trusted-caller parameters: section 4's memory-safety requirement covers paths carrying data from other parties, and the library stand-in rule rates by components that reach the defect, so a heap over-read reachable by any future caller rates Low today (R6-DYNAPI-1).
